scope: finite legacy FTS5 custom tokenizer callback interface
statements: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE docs USING fts5(body,tokenize='testspace')
INSERT INTO docs(rowid,body) VALUES(1,'red  blue'),(2,'blue green'),(3,'red green blue')
SELECT rowid,highlight(docs,0,'[',']') AS marked FROM docs WHERE docs MATCH 'red' ORDER BY rowid
SELECT rowid,snippet(docs,0,'[',']','...',8) AS excerpt FROM docs WHERE docs MATCH 'bl*' ORDER BY rowid
UPDATE docs SET body='green blue' WHERE rowid=1
SELECT rowid,body FROM docs WHERE docs MATCH 'red' ORDER BY rowid
SELECT rowid,highlight(docs,0,'[',']') AS marked FROM docs WHERE docs MATCH 'green' ORDER BY rowid
limits: One in-memory connection, legacy fts5_tokenizer registration, fixed lowercase ASCII words split only on byte 0x20.
Original input byte slices and offsets are passed to the engine xToken callback synchronously; no borrowed input/context survives the callback.
Tokenizer owners are released once through xDelete; registration context/event counters remain alive until sqlite3_close returns.
Exact rows, callback flags, token offsets, callback order and owner/destructor counts come from the separate pinned native oracle.
A nonzero engine xToken result is propagated immediately; this successful SQL slice does not force an engine callback error.
Locale/v2 tokenizer, synonyms, Unicode rules, custom auxiliary functions, FTS3 tokenizer interfaces and broader failure/ownership cases remain separate.
